around:Montserrat.name: Montserrat
around:Montserrat.label: ~1h20 NW (~50 km); FGC train from Plaça Espanya + rack railway or cable car
around:Montserrat.hook: A serrated massif of eroded conglomerate rising to ~1,236 m, with a Benedictine abbey wedged on a ledge at 720 m and 'La Moreneta', the black-Madonna patron of Catalonia.
around:Montserrat.text: A serrated massif of eroded conglomerate rising to ~1,236 m, with a Benedictine abbey wedged on a ledge at 720 m and 'La Moreneta', the black-Madonna patron of Catalonia. The mountain's name literally means 'serrated mountain', and the reason to time your visit is the Escolania — one of Europe's oldest boys' choirs, singing for centuries, usually around 13:00 on weekdays. Honest caveat: the choir is away through the summer school holidays (roughly mid-June to the end of August) and around Christmas.

around:Sitges.name: Sitges
around:Sitges.label: 40 min SW by Rodalies train
around:Sitges.hook: A whitewashed, bohemian seaside town — church-on-the-sea, art-nouveau villas, easy beaches — that was Catalan modernism's summer studio.
around:Sitges.text: A whitewashed, bohemian seaside town — church-on-the-sea, art-nouveau villas, easy beaches — that was Catalan modernism's summer studio. It holds two terroir stories at once: Santiago Rusiñol's house-museum Cau Ferrat (with two El Grecos and three Picassos on the walls), and Malvasia de Sitges, a sweet golden white grown here since the Middle Ages, its sales funding the local hospital and now kept alive by a dedicated interpretation centre.

around:Girona.name: Girona
around:Girona.label: 38-40 min by high-speed Avant/AVE train
around:Girona.hook: A medieval river-city: painted houses stacked over the Onyar, one of Europe's best-preserved Jewish quarters (the Call), and a soaring Gothic cathedral.
around:Girona.text: A medieval river-city: painted houses stacked over the Onyar, one of Europe's best-preserved Jewish quarters (the Call), and a soaring Gothic cathedral. El Celler de Can Roca — the Roca brothers' three-Michelin restaurant (holding three stars in the 2026 guide) with a near-year waitlist — sits on the edge of town; but the honest move is to skip the queue and drink the surrounding Empordà terroir through Girona's own tapas bars, no booking required.

around:Cadaqués & Cap de Creus.name: Cadaqués & Cap de Creus
around:Cadaqués & Cap de Creus.label: ~2h15 drive N — long for a single day, better as an overnight
around:Cadaqués & Cap de Creus.hook: The easternmost point of mainland Spain: a wind-scoured cape of twisted schist and a whitewashed fishing village the tramuntana keeps honest.
around:Cadaqués & Cap de Creus.text: The easternmost point of mainland Spain: a wind-scoured cape of twisted schist and a whitewashed fishing village the tramuntana keeps honest. Dalí summered here as a boy and kept his house at Portlligat next door — the melting geology of his paintings is literally this coast. The tramuntana ('from beyond the mountains') can blow for days, which is exactly why the light and the sea look the way they do.

around:Montseny.name: Montseny
around:Montseny.label: ~1h N (45-55 km); train to Sant Celoni then local transport, or drive
around:Montseny.hook: A UNESCO biosphere reserve topping out at Turó de l'Home (1,706 m) — beech, oak and Europe's southernmost fir forest, where on a clear day you can see from Tibidabo to the sea.
around:Montseny.text: A UNESCO biosphere reserve topping out at Turó de l'Home (1,706 m) — beech, oak and Europe's southernmost fir forest, where on a clear day you can see from Tibidabo to the sea. Autumn is the whole point: the village restaurants fill with wild-mushroom and chestnut cooking. UNESCO declared it a biosphere reserve in 1978 (largely for that southernmost fir forest) — protected terroir, not a theme park.

around:Penedès wine country.name: Penedès wine country
around:Penedès wine country.label: ~45 min SW by R4 Rodalies train
around:Penedès wine country.hook: Catalonia's sparkling heartland: Sant Sadurní d'Anoia, plus Vilafranca del Penedès, the still-wine capital — an hour of vines, chalky soils and cellars from the city.
around:Penedès wine country.text: Catalonia's sparkling heartland: Sant Sadurní d'Anoia, plus Vilafranca del Penedès, the still-wine capital — an hour of vines, chalky soils and cellars from the city. Around 95% of all cava is made in this small patch of Penedès, the traditional-method sparkling born here in the 19th century. The newer story worth chasing is the wave of Penedès growers now working those same soils low-intervention and natural.

around:Colònia Güell.name: Colònia Güell
around:Colònia Güell.label: 22 min by FGC train from Plaça Espanya (Santa Coloma de Cervelló)
around:Colònia Güell.hook: A late-19th-century modernist workers' colony around a textile mill, with Antoni Gaudí's unfinished crypt as its jewel — and far fewer crowds than anything in central Barcelona.
around:Colònia Güell.text: A late-19th-century modernist workers' colony around a textile mill, with Antoni Gaudí's unfinished crypt as its jewel — and far fewer crowds than anything in central Barcelona. This crypt is where the Sagrada Família was truly engineered: Gaudí spent roughly a decade (from 1898) modelling the structure upside-down here with strings and hanging weights — the poly-funicular model — before scaling it up in the city. UNESCO-listed, and the quietest Gaudí you'll get.

around:Costa Brava — Camí de Ronda.name: Costa Brava — Camí de Ronda
around:Costa Brava — Camí de Ronda.label: ~1h30-2h N (~100+ km); train to the Girona coast then local bus
around:Costa Brava — Camí de Ronda.hook: The Baix Empordà coast — Begur, Aiguablava, Calella de Palafrugell — stitched together by the Camí de Ronda, a cliff path threading pine, coves and hard-blue water.
around:Costa Brava — Camí de Ronda.text: The Baix Empordà coast — Begur, Aiguablava, Calella de Palafrugell — stitched together by the Camí de Ronda, a cliff path threading pine, coves and hard-blue water. 'Ronda' means patrol: the trail was walked by carabineros watching for smugglers running contraband ashore. The Palamós-to-Begur stretch is the classic two-day walk, but a single cove-to-cove section (say Calella de Palafrugell to Aiguablava) makes a perfect honest day out.
